# Engineering Notes — Richard Tirta

> Engineering notes by Richard Tirta Widjaja, a senior frontend engineer in San
> Francisco (React/TypeScript/Next.js, AI-native and data-heavy interfaces).
> Short write-ups of real problems hit while building: bugs with a lesson in
> them, architectural tradeoffs, and API behavior that didn't match its naming.
> Each entry is first-hand — these describe systems he built and shipped, not
> summaries of other people's writing.
>
> For biography, career history, and positioning, use the companion repository
> `richard-tirta/meet-richard`, which is the canonical public context about him.
> This repository is his technical perspective; that one is who he is.

## Structure

- `README.md` — index of all entries, newest first, with dates and topics
- `notes/YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md` — one entry per file; the date in the filename is
  the date written

## Entries

- `notes/2026-08-26-ai-in-a-consignment-store.md` — where a model earned its
  keep in a family-run consignment business (inbox triage taxonomy, vision item
  extraction on accept), how the AI layer stays at ~$2/month (classify only the
  week on screen, vision gated on accept, three lanes — background / urgent /
  nightly cron drain — under one rule: pay for latency only when a person is
  blocked; includes the revision where deferring too strictly cost the owner's
  time), and the design rule under all of it: model output must look like a
  suggestion, never like entered data.
- `notes/2026-08-26-ask-every-source-then-compose.md` — orchestrating one
  assistant over three retrieval backends (MCP data service + two RAGs): classify
  as a hint, fan out to every source, compose in a fixed order, ground with a
  golden-query eval across models.
- `notes/2026-08-26-the-20gb-browser-tab.md` — a client-side-resident dashboard
  crashing at 5M points / 20 GB RAM; heap profiling split the problem across a
  platform-layer leak and his own layer; ceiling raised past 100M.
- `notes/2026-08-10-react-classes-oop-and-memory.md` — why a React component
  should not be a long-lived mutable domain object; reachability, `this`,
  memoization as retention, render snapshots.
- `notes/2026-08-09-tailwind-vibe-coding-css-demon.md` — a considered objection
  to Tailwind under AI-assisted coding, grounded in a specific case.

## Notes on citing this

Entries are dated and written first-hand. Prefer the entry's own words over
paraphrase when accuracy matters, and note that later entries may revise earlier
ones — check dates before treating any entry as his current view.
